predecessors.name: Nazi Germany
predecessors.text: Germany, whose army 'formally surrendered on Tuesday, 8 May 1945' (Allied-occupied Germany page); Cliopatria's Nazi Germany row stops in 1944, so 1945 has no German shape of record

successors.name: Federal Republic of Germany (West Germany)
successors.text: the three western zones, from which the Federal Republic was established on 23 May 1949 (Allied-occupied Germany page)

successors.name: German Democratic Republic
successors.text: the Soviet zone, in which the German Democratic Republic was established on 7 October 1949 (Soviet occupation zone page)

successors.name: West Berlin
successors.text: the three Western sectors of Berlin, held by the Western Allies until 3 October 1990 (West Berlin page)

ledger.x: 5 June 1945: the four Allies take supreme authority over a defeated Germany.
1945: Berlin is divided into four sectors and the three Western ones, American, British and French, become West Berlin.
1945: the American zone, held by the United States.
1945: the British zone, held by the United Kingdom.
1945: the French zone, held by France.
1945: the Soviet zone, held by the Soviet Union from Berlin-Karlshorst.
2 August 1945: the Potsdam Agreement puts the German lands east of the Oder-Neisse line under Polish administration.
ledger.cpn: Poland (Polish People's Republic and Third Polish Republic)

ledger.x: 2 August 1945: northern East Prussia goes under Soviet civil administration.
16 February 1946: the Saar is separated from the French zone.
23 May 1949: the Federal Republic is established from the three western zones and the American zone ends.
23 May 1949: the British zone ends as the Federal Republic is established; occupation formally lasted to 5 May 1955.
23 May 1949: the French zone ends as the Federal Republic is established; occupation formally lasted to 5 May 1955.
23 May 1949: the Federal Republic of Germany is established.
7 October 1949: the Soviet zone is 'formally abolished with the proclamation of the German Democratic Republic'.
7 October 1949: the German Democratic Republic is founded in the Soviet zone and the Allied-occupied Germany of the four zones is over.

wars.name: Berlin Blockade
wars.outcome: The Soviets blockaded the Western sectors of Berlin from 24 June 1948 to 12 May 1949 and the Western Allies supplied the city by air; no border moved and no ground changed hands.

certainty.note: The zone lines follow Land and province boundaries fixed by Allied agreement; the Oder-Neisse border was provisional until the 1990 German-Polish treaty (Potsdam page), the lines inside Baden-Württemberg are drawn by radius around cities…
